en: A pulley system reduces the effort force needed to lift a heavy box, but it does not change the total amount of work done.
Static friction prevents stationary objects, like a heavy refrigerator resting on a ramp, from starting to move until the pushing force overcomes it.
In a vacuum without air resistance, gravity accelerates a heavy bowling ball and a light feather downward at the exact same rate.
Magnets do not only attract iron; they also strongly attract other ferromagnetic metals like nickel, cobalt, and specific steel alloys.
A battery does not create new electrons; it simply provides the voltage needed to push existing free electrons through a copper wire.
Light does not travel instantaneously; it moves at a finite speed of about 300,000 kilometers per second through empty space.
Sound waves require a physical medium like air, water, or solid wood to travel, meaning they cannot move through the vacuum of space.
Heat and temperature are different; heat is the transferred thermal energy between objects, while temperature measures the average kinetic energy of particles.
When a moving bicycle brakes to a stop, its kinetic energy is not destroyed but transformed into thermal energy via brake pad friction.
A third-class lever, like a human forearm or a pair of tweezers, multiplies distance and speed rather than multiplying the input force.
If you break a bar magnet in half, you do not get isolated poles; each new piece instantly forms its own north and south pole.
Electric current is not used up by a light bulb; the exact same amount of current flowing in also flows out of it.
